To give you a bit background info, the same survey items measuring a particular construct were given to the same people over 3 time points. The indicators are ordinal. When I tested scalar invariance (without the intercept and slope part excluded) using cfa(), the model fit was very good. But when I tried to do growth curve modeling by using growth() (after adding the two lines for latent intercept and slope), I got the warnings show below. I wonder how I can potentially solve the problem. (Also, to deal with missing data, I used missing="pairwise"). 

In lav_model_vcov(lavmodel = lavmodel, lavsamplestats = lavsamplestats,  ... :
  lavaan WARNING: could not compute standard errors!
  lavaan NOTE: this may be a symptom that the model is not identified.


In lav_model_test(lavmodel = lavmodel, lavpartable = lavpartable,  ... :
  lavaan WARNING: could not compute scaled test statistic


Thanks in advance!

DIsclosure warning: I'm very new to lavaan.
Having said that, in order to have the model be identified, don't you need to set one of the indicators of ft1, ft2, and ft3 to 1 so that the model is identified. Because this is part of a larger hierarchical factor model, you can't set the disturbance variance to 1. Just a thought and hope it helps. Phil Wood

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Growth curve model with the unidentified model warning
parts:
On 04/04/2015 02:13 PM, Xiao He wrote:
> Dear all,
>
> I am trying to do growth curve modeling with the following model:

As a general comment: the 'growth()' function of lavaan was only
designed for

1) growth-in-the-observed-variables setting (not growth in the latent
variables), and

2) continuous observed variables.

(I seriously consider removing it from lavaan 0.6, but adding a new
operator instead that defines random effects.)

I would recommend using the lavaan() function for this, perhaps in
combination with some auto.*= arguments. (see ?lavaan)

So, try to code the growth model in such a way that you are very
explicit about every parameter that you need in the model, use the
lavaan() function, and that should do it.

Yves.
